title: Separate disposable compute from durable state
description: Size the documented HDFS replication model, choose the data authority, and inject a primary, core, or task-node interruption to see the operational consequence.
modelNote: The HDFS capacity estimate follows the AWS formula: core-node storage multiplied by core-node count, divided by the configured replication factor. The displayed factors are AWS defaults by core-node count. Filesystem overhead, EBS behavior, block placement, decommissioning, concurrent failures, and custom Hadoop settings require separate measurement and validation.

storageModes.label: Amazon S3 is authoritative
storageModes.detail: Inputs, checkpoints, and committed outputs survive cluster replacement.
storageModes.authority: Durable state lives outside the cluster

storageModes.label: Cluster HDFS is authoritative
storageModes.detail: Required data depends on core nodes and the cluster's HDFS metadata and replicas.
storageModes.authority: Required state depends on this cluster

incidents.label: Lose a primary node
incidents.detail: Interrupt cluster coordination and primary services.
incidents.computeEffect: A single-primary cluster ends when its primary terminates.
incidents.hdfsEffect: HDFS coordination becomes unavailable with the failed cluster.
incidents.recovery: A three-primary cluster can fail over to a standby and replace the failed node.

incidents.label: Lose a core node
incidents.detail: Remove compute plus an HDFS DataNode.
incidents.computeEffect: Executor capacity falls and active work may need recomputation.
incidents.hdfsEffect: Blocks and transient shuffle on the node are lost; required HDFS data may become unavailable.
incidents.recovery: Restore capacity, let HDFS repair replicas where possible, and retry from external checkpoints.

incidents.label: Lose a task node
incidents.detail: Remove compute that stores no HDFS blocks.
incidents.computeEffect: Executor capacity falls and tasks may retry on surviving workers.
incidents.hdfsEffect: The interrupted task node held no persistent HDFS data.
incidents.recovery: Replace or scale task capacity and allow retry-safe work to continue.
